sheet-1.description: The lower half of the title sheet of the November 1924 Park Ridge atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, larger than the rest of the volume at 100 feet. It covers the business and industrial centre of the borough between Maple Avenue at the top and Railroad Avenue at the bottom, from Mittag Place on the west to Park Avenue and Market Street on the east. The railroad of the New Jersey and New York Railroad (Erie Line) crosses the bottom of the sheet diagonally, with the passenger station and freight house east of Park Avenue. Most of the area is taken up by the Mittag and Volger Manufacturing Company works for carbon papers and typewriter ribbons, a long brick and frame plant with boiler house, cutting and grinding rooms, a laboratory and a roll paper warehouse, drawn with details of its watchmen, power, lighting and hydrants. North of the works, along Maple Avenue, are frame dwellings on large lots. On the corner of Park Avenue stands the post office with a drug store, and east of Park Avenue a block between Maple Avenue, Market Street and Hawthorne Avenue holds a boarding house and stores, with a small oval park south of Hawthorne Avenue. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are drawn along the streets. Woodland, Roland and Perryland Streets are lettered at the bottom edge where they leave Railroad Avenue southward; they are drawn in full on sheet 4. The upper half of the sheet, with the key map at 1000 feet to an inch, the index and the water and fire notes, is not part of this map.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Broadway; Maple Avenue is now North Maple Avenue east of Park Avenue and South Maple Avenue west of it.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the other sheets of the volume are at 100 feet.
Mittag and Volger Manufacturing Company, carbon papers and typewriter ribbons, fills most of the sheet.

Title page with key map (1000 ft to an inch, not georeferenced), state inset, water and fire notes and street index in the upper half; lower half is a 50 ft map of Maple Av, Mittag Pl, Park Av, Market St, Hawthorne Av and Railroad Av (Mittag and Volger carbon paper works, post office, station). One part (the lower map). Key notes 7 sheets; sheets 6 and 7 (Montvale) are not in this record.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the west side of Park Ridge along Main Street (today Pascack Road) from a cemetery at the west edge to Ridge Avenue on the east, and a strip northward along Ridge Avenue to 5th Street. Most of the area is open land in large sections (Sec. 7 and Sec. 9) with scattered frame dwellings, outbuildings and a water tower, and it is drawn sparsely. The Paskack Reform Church stands on the south side of Main Street with a cemetery south and west of it. At the east end, between Main Street, Park Avenue and Storms Avenue, the Park Ridge Public School is drawn with its gymnasium and auditorium, and small blocks of dwellings line Park Avenue and Storms Avenue down to Willet Street at the bottom edge, where Pascack Brook enters the corner. Mill Road leaves Storms Avenue eastward. Along Ridge Avenue north of Main Street are house lots, the First Congregational Church and a few outbuildings, and at the top right a row of lots along 5th Street. A heavy line marks off the upper left corner of the sheet, which is drawn separately as part 2; the dash-dot match line A-B at the left edge joins this part to it. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Main Street, Park Avenue and Ridge Avenue.
notes: Main is now Pascack Road; 5th Street is now South 5th Street west of Ridge Avenue.
Willet is labelled 'Willet (Storms Av.)'; it is now Willet Street.
The Cemetery south of Main Street belongs to the Paskack Reform Church (spelled so on the sheet).
Placement rests on control points at the east end only (Park Avenue to Ridge Avenue); the cemetery end is extrapolated.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (L-shaped main map) Main St (now Pascack Road) from the cemetery to Ridge Av, Park Av, Storms Av, Mill Rd, Willet (Storms Av), 5th St and Ridge Av; part 2 (upper left, behind a heavy line, match line A-B) Main St west from Glen Rd with Hillside Av, East Av and Hill. Part 2 placed from Glen Rd and Hillside Av junctions and a point carried from part 1 at the match line (helmert, scale_ft 96.1 so the second pass keeps it on the carried point).

sheet-2-2.description: The upper left corner of sheet 2, set off from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It continues Main Street (today Pascack Road) westward from the dash-dot match line A-B, which joins it to the west edge of part 1 of the same sheet, to Glen Road at the borough limits, where the Borough of Woodcliff Lake begins. North of Main Street are open land in Sec. 6 and Sec. 7, a few dwellings and hen houses, and a strip marked Right of Way; south of Main Street a block of Sec. 9 is bounded by Hillside Avenue, East Avenue and Hill, with a large lot numbered 117 and a few dwellings, the rest of the strip to the match line being cemetery land. Water pipes and a hydrant are drawn along Main Street and an alarm tire stands at Glen Road. The area is thinly built and drawn with few buildings.
notes: Main is now Pascack Road.
East Avenue and Hill are not in the modern street data.
Placed from two street junctions and a point carried from part 1 at the match line, all along Main Street; low confidence.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the residential north side of Park Ridge from Ridge Avenue on the west to Cascade Avenue on the east, between 5th Street and Arbor Place at the top and Main Street (today Pascack Road) near the bottom, and a strip south of Main Street along Mill Lane and Mill Road to Pascack Brook and the mill pond. The district is laid out in narrow house lots, many still vacant, on Ridge, North, Louville, Midland, Mountain, Colony and Lakeview Avenues and the cross streets Randolph, Echo Place, Summit, Lafayette Avenue and Lawn. Mill Brook runs through the west half of the sheet from top to bottom, crossing Main Street, and Crescent follows a curve beside it at the top. Colony Avenue has a turning circle near Randolph, and a second circle lies off Summit. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings with some brick or stone houses and a few stores on Main Street. South of Main Street are larger tracts of Sec. 8 with an electric generator at the dam of Pascack Brook, where the brook widens into the pond. Willet and the southern Mill Road appear at the bottom left corner. A compass rose and the bar scale are drawn in the open land south of Main Street.
notes: Main is now Pascack Road.
5th Street, South Arbor Place and Arbor Place are now one street, North 5th Street.
Lafayette Avenue is now Lafayette Street; Victor Hugo is Victor Hugo Street; Randolph is Randolph Street; Lawn is Lawn Street; Cascade is Cascade Avenue; Willet is Willet Street.
Summit is now Summit Avenue east of Colony Avenue and Summit Street west of it; Summit Street west of Mountain Avenue is not drawn in 1924.
Crescent is not in the modern street data.

100 ft. Main St (Pascack Road) north side from Ridge Av to Cascade Av: 5th St, North Av, Louville, Midland, Mountain, Colony, Lakeview Avs, Arbor Pl, Echo Pl, Randolph, Summit, Lafayette, Victor Hugo, Lawn, Etheridge Pl, Cascade; south of Main: Mill Lane, Mill Rd, Pascack Brook and pond. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the southwest part of Park Ridge south of the railroad of the New Jersey and New York Railroad (Erie Line). At the top, north of the tracks, Maple Avenue and Mittag Place bound the Park Ridge Paper Box Company works and a lumber shed. Railroad Avenue runs along the south side of the tracks, and the streets Highland, Oakland, Vineland, Woodland, Roland and Perryland run south from it, crossed by Terrace, to Magnolia Avenue, which crosses the sheet from Highland to Park Avenue at the east edge. The blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, many vacant, with frame dwellings, a fire department house on Roland, stores near Park Avenue and the public library at Magnolia Avenue and Park Avenue. South of Magnolia Avenue, Morningside Avenue runs diagonally southeast with the short streets Alexander, Bogert, Kelsic, Ormsay, Lillian and Local leaving it to the southwest, an area of small lots and few buildings. Chestnut Avenue runs east from Morningside Avenue to Park Avenue. Large open tracts (Sec. 10, Sec. 11 and Sec. 12) fill the west and south, and Rivervale Road and Rock Avenue meet at the bottom edge, with a church for coloured people nearby. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along most streets.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Broadway; Magnolia Avenue is now Kinderkamack Road; Chestnut Avenue is now Chestnut Street.
Highland, Terrace, Oakland, Woodland, Roland, Perryland, Kelsic, Ormsay, Lillian and Local are now Streets of those names; Alexander is Alexander Street.
Vineland and Bogert are not in the modern street data.
Hawthorn Avenue (spelled so) is lettered at the top right edge; it is drawn on sheets 1 and 5.
Park Avenue / Rivervale Road at the east edge was left out of the control: only one side of the junction is drawn.

100 ft. Pilot. Railroad Av (now Broadway), Magnolia Av (now Kinderkamack Road), Highland, Terrace, Oakland, Vineland, Woodland, Roland, Perryland, Park Av, Chestnut, Morningside, Alexander, Bogert, Kelsic, Ormsay, Lillian, Local, Rivervale Rd, Rock Av; Park Ridge Paper Box Co. One part.

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the east side of central Park Ridge from Park Avenue eastward to Ajax Alley and the borough line, and from Willet and Pascack Creek at the top to Highview Avenue at the bottom. At the top left the fire department chemical company house stands on Willet, with a carpenter shop and the Park Ridge pumping station on Park Avenue beside Pascack Creek; a mill race and a pond cross the open land of Sec. 8 to the north. Below them lie residential blocks on Maple Avenue, Linden Avenue, Market, Madison and Hawthorne Avenue, with St. Mary's R.C. Church near Ajax Alley. The railroad of the New Jersey and New York Railroad (Erie Line) crosses the sheet diagonally, with a coal shed and stores beside it near Perry. South of the tracks is the main shopping street, Magnolia Avenue, with stores, Forester Hall, the Star Motion Picture Theatre and a public garage, and further south Chestnut Avenue and Highview Avenue with dwellings, open lots and the Park Ridge M. E. Church. Perry and Berthoud cross Magnolia Avenue. Rivervale Road is lettered at the bottom left corner and the line between the Borough of Park Ridge and the neighbouring borough runs down the bottom right corner. An inset at the upper right (part 2) shows the W. H. Dean Company apron factory on Mill Road and is not part of this map.
notes: Magnolia Avenue is now Kinderkamack Road; Maple Avenue is now North Maple Avenue; Chestnut Avenue is now Chestnut Street; Railroad Avenue is now Broadway.
Market, Madison, Perry and Berthoud are now Market Street, Madison Avenue, Perry Street and Berthoud Street; Willet is Willet Street.
Ajax Alley is not in the modern street data.
Perry south of Magnolia Avenue runs on a different line from Perry north of it, as today.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Park Av, Maple, Market, Madison, Hawthorne, Linden, Perry, Berthoud, Ajax Alley, Magnolia (now Kinderkamack Road), Chestnut, Highview, pumping station, St. Mary's R.C. Church; part 2 (inset, upper right) W. H. Dean Co. apron factory on Mill Rd by the pond, own north arrow.
